title: A Hardware-Native Trapped-Ion Hybrid Qudit-Oscillator Instruction Set
authors: Masoud Hakimi Heris, Yuan Liu, Frank Mueller
abstract: Scaling trapped-ion processors by adding ions remains challenging. A complementary route exploits the multilevel internal structure of each ion to increase the computational Hilbert space per ion. We introduce a hardware-native hybrid qudit-oscillator instruction set for a general d-level internal register coupled to bosonic modes and prove that three of its native operation families suffice for universality of one qudit coupled to several modes. Adding an entangling operation between ions extends universality to a connected register of several qudits. The architecture natively supports both phase-space and sideband instruction sets and is implemented in the open-source framework HybridLane. As a representative application, we reproduce the dissipative vibronic dynamics of a three-chromophore complex previously simulated on a hybrid qubit-oscillator superconducting platform. Moving from a one-qubit-per-state register to a single qudit stores the entire electronic manifold in one ion, so every electronic coupling becomes a local intra-ion transition and the lab-frame Hamiltonian compiles directly into the ISA. Under the stated sequential timing model from a 40Ca+ qudit processor, one Trotter step is projected to run about ten times faster on the qudit, with an average RMSE of approximately 1.1 percent against the published reference.
summary: This paper proposes a novel hardware-native instruction set for trapped-ion quantum computers by utilizing the multilevel structure of individual ions as qudits. By encoding the entire electronic manifold into one ion, the authors simplify Hamiltonian mapping and demonstrate a projected ten-fold speedup over traditional qubit-based encoding for simulating complex molecular dynamics.
main_problem: Scaling trapped-ion quantum processors is challenging; the authors propose using the multilevel structure of individual ions (qudits) to increase computational capacity per ion.
main_result: They introduce a hardware-native instruction set for qudit-oscillator coupling, demonstrating that this approach can project a ten-fold speedup for Trotter steps compared to traditional qubit-only encoding.
method: The work involves defining a set of hardware-native ISA primitives (e.g., qudit phase shift, level-conditioned displacement) and developing a timing model to project gate execution times.
model_or_system: The system is a trapped-ion hybrid qudit-oscillator processor, coupling a general d-level internal register (qudit) to bosonic motional modes. The architecture allows the entire electronic manifold to be stored in one ion, simplifying Hamiltonian mapping.
key_observables: Average Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 1.1% when reproducing vibronic dynamics; projected speedup factor of ~10 for Trotter steps.
important_parameters: The system uses a $^{40}	ext{Ca}^+$ qudit processor; key parameters include detunings ($\delta$) and various Rabi/drive frequencies.
main_assumptions: The timing model assumes a sequential scheduling of gates, and the speedup projection relies on the qudit encoding being superior to the qubit encoding for the given task.
figures_summary: Figures conceptually illustrate the qudit-oscillator coupling within the instruction set, while tables detail the five native ISA primitives and the timing costs for qubit vs. qudit encodings.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the qudit concept to overcome scaling limits, details the five fundamental hardware-native ISA primitives, proves the universality of a subset of these primitives, and finally validates the approach by simulating a complex vibronic dynamics problem and analyzing the resulting timing model.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the hardware limitations of trapped-ion quantum computing by proposing a sophisticated, physically grounded ISA that leverages internal electronic structure, which is highly relevant for AMO physicists working on quantum simulation.
